summary: The bill expands the Miccosukee Reserved Area in Everglades National Park to include Osceola Camp and requires the Interior Secretary, within two years, to take steps to protect structures there from flooding.

scores.thoughts: The bill mandates federal action to protect structures from flooding but contains no appropriations, funding mechanisms, or policy directives on overall government spending levels. It does not expand or reduce spending in any programmatic sense.
The bill makes no reference to taxes, tax policy, rates, or revenue measures of any kind.
No provisions relate to healthcare delivery, insurance, public coverage, or market-based reforms.
The legislation has no connection to firearms, regulations, or gun rights.
No content addresses immigration pathways, border enforcement, or related protections.
The bill contains nothing regarding reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions involve military or defense spending or policy.

The bill concerns land within Everglades National Park and flood protection measures but does not expand environmental regulations, create new protections, or limit regulatory authority; it is a narrow, site-specific tribal land adjustment.
No provisions relate to welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety net policies.
The bill does not address schools, education funding, or school choice.
No content pertains to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related policies.
The legislation has no bearing on sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions involve trade, tariffs, or globalization.
The bill does not address deficit spending, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No content relates to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
The bill contains no provisions on foreign aid.
No provisions address voting access, election integrity, or related reforms.
The legislation does not engage with technology regulation or data privacy.
No content pertains to worker protections, unions, or employer flexibility.
The bill does not address religious exemptions or civil rights priorities.
